summary: Iteration 70: UTM attribution + FB photo posts. Backend pytest 26/26 pass (click endpoint, signup_source sanitising on register, admin report shape/auth for facebook|instagram|all x 7|30|90, share_post __PLATFORM__ replacement via a fake adapter, recruit broadcast URL, _post_facebook /photos then /feed fallback with mocked httpx, and a real Graph call with a fake token returning 400 OAuthException). Frontend e2e passes: a UTM visit stores lumo_attr (first touch is kept when a later instagram visit happens), POSTs /attribution/click once (a reload does not double count), and a customer signup through the Register UI saves user.signup_source with lowercased values. Admin Recruit tab shows admin-recruit-results above the city blog panel; stat cards, post/city tables and selects work, and each select change fires a refetch.

minor.issue: totals.signups and posts[].signups count users of every role (the test customers are counted), but cities[].signups and from_source count only providers. The user's goal is new contractors, so the post numbers overstate contractor signups. Suggest adding role=provider to those counts or returning a separate provider count.

City from_source needs users.recruit_city_slug, which is only set by the /join apply flow. A provider who lands on /join/{city}/blog/... and then signs up through plain /register gets signup_source.landing_path but no recruit_city_slug, so the city is never credited. Suggest falling back to the city taken from landing_path.
totals.posts_shared counts city_blog_posts.fb_shared_at whatever source is selected, so the 'Posts shared to FB' card shows a Facebook number even when Instagram is picked. Only a labelling issue.
Public and unauthenticated with no rate limit or dedupe, so anyone can inflate click counts with a script. Minor.

5 of 19 city_blog_posts use hero_image on host thumb.wikimedia.org (3840px). Wikimedia returned 403 'bot-traffic' to the facebookexternalhit UA from this container, for both upload.* and thumb.* URLs (a browser UA got 200). If FB's crawler is also blocked, /photos fails and the post silently falls back to a link post, which works but loses the big image. Worth checking the first real prod post, or re-hosting images on our own storage or CDN.

issues: While the report loads, the panel shows only the header with no loading or error state. If the request fails it is caught and the data silently set to null.
